title: Size-independent Logarithmic Sobolev Inequalities for Quantum Gibbs Samplers
authors: Hongrui Chen, Zhiyan Ding, Jianfeng Lu
abstract: We propose a new method for proving $L^2$ and modified logarithmic Sobolev inequalities with constants independent of system size for quantum Gibbs samplers whose Lindblad generators satisfy Kubo-Martin-Schwinger (KMS) detailed balance. We first establish the $L^2$ logarithmic Sobolev inequality by transporting it along a temperature-dependent path from the infinite-temperature product state to the target Gibbs state while maintaining a size-independent decay rate for the sandwiched Rényi-2 divergence. A tensor-power argument, combined with the quantum asymptotic equipartition property, then transfers this decay bound to relative entropy, yielding the modified logarithmic Sobolev inequality. This approach provides a general framework for proving size-independent logarithmic Sobolev inequalities for quantum Gibbs samplers. We apply it to two regimes: one-dimensional quantum spin chains at every finite temperature, and finite-range quantum spin systems at sufficiently high temperature in any fixed dimension.
summary: This paper develops a novel mathematical framework to prove size-independent Logarithmic Sobolev Inequalities for quantum Gibbs samplers. By transporting an L2 LSI along a unitary path from infinite temperature, the authors derive bounds for the relative entropy, which are essential for proving rapid mixing times in quantum spin systems. This advances the theoretical understanding of thermalization dynamics in quantum many-body systems.
main_problem: The central goal is to establish size-independent Logarithmic Sobolev Inequalities (LSI) and Modified Logarithmic Sobolev Inequalities (MLSI) for quantum Gibbs samplers.
main_result: The authors propose a general framework that achieves size-independent bounds for both L2 LSI and MLSI for quantum Gibbs samplers in specific regimes (e.g., 1D at any temperature, or higher dimensions at high temperature).
method: The core technique involves transporting an L2 LSI from an infinite-temperature product state to the target Gibbs state along a temperature-dependent unitary path, analogous to classical transport maps.
model_or_system: The study focuses on quantum Gibbs samplers whose Lindblad generators satisfy Kubo-Martin-Schwinger (KMS) detailed balance, applied to quantum spin chains (both 1D and finite-range systems).
key_observables: L2 relative entropy, sandwiched Rényi-2 divergence, and the relative entropy itself, which are used to diagnose the rate of convergence.
important_parameters: The analysis depends on the inverse temperature ($ eta$), the spatial dimension ($d$), and the system size ($n$), with the key result being the independence of the bounds on $n$.
main_assumptions: The generator $L$ must be primitive and KMS-symmetric. The method relies on the existence of a unitary path connecting the infinite-temperature state to the Gibbs state.
paper_structure: The paper develops the framework by first establishing the L2 LSI via unitary path transport, then using a tensor-power argument to transfer this bound to the relative entropy (MLSI). Subsequent sections apply this framework to prove the inequalities for specific physical regimes (1D and high-temperature).
why_interesting: This work provides a powerful, general mathematical tool for proving rapid mixing bounds in quantum many-body systems, which is crucial for understanding thermalization and quantum dynamics in condensed matter physics.
